program.title: Football Winger – Hamstring Resilience & Single-Leg Power (Week 1)
program.goal: Build eccentric hamstring strength, single-leg control, and sprint-ready tissue capacity for winger acceleration and deceleration

athlete_analysis.profile_summary: Intermediate football winger with previous hamstring tightness. Trains 1 session/week in a gym with barbell, dumbbells, sled, and turf access. Moderate stress, good sleep. Goals: sport performance and running speed.
primary_constraints: Previous hamstring tightness requires conservative loading and eccentric emphasis
Single session per week demands multi-purpose work: strength, power, and tissue capacity in one session
Winger role needs unilateral lower-body control and lateral hip strength for dribbling and cutting
sport_demands: Hamstring resilience: eccentric strength, sprint mechanics, and lumbopelvic control
Single-leg acceleration and deceleration from varied angles
Hip abduction and adductor capacity for lateral movement and cutting
athlete_analysis.block_priority: Preseason tissue-capacity ramp: restore sprint mechanics, eccentric hamstring load, and position-specific single-leg power. Progress conservatively given previous tightness; avoid high-volume sprinting until base strength is confirmed pain-free.

weeks.theme: Hamstring eccentric foundation and single-leg plant strength for winger power

workouts.title: Hamstring Eccentric, Single-Leg Strength & Hip Stability
sport_transfer: Unilateral leg strength for acceleration plant and cutting deceleration
Hip stability during dribbling and change-of-direction maneuvers
Hamstring resilience for sprint exposure progression next week
workouts.why_this_session: Eccentric and single-leg work restores hamstring confidence and builds side-to-side control without max-effort sprinting. Conservative load respects previous tightness while priming nervous system and tissue for power.

warmup.name: Bird Dog
warmup.purpose: Activate lumbopelvic control and stabilizer muscles before lower-body loading

warmup.name: Front-Back Leg Swing
warmup.purpose: Dynamic hip and hamstring mobility preparation for lower-body work

warmup.name: Dead Bug
warmup.purpose: Supine core stability without spinal load; reinforce neutral spine before lifting

main_work.name: B-Stance Romanian Deadlift
main_work.purpose: Build eccentric hamstring and posterior-chain strength with single-leg bias; safe alternative to true single-leg RDL
main_work.load_guidance: Dumbbell or kettlebell; start light (5–10 kg per hand). Emphasize eccentric 3-sec lowering and pain-free range. If tightness appears mid-set, stop and assess.

main_work.name: Single-Leg Leg Press
main_work.purpose: Machine-supported single-leg strength and stability; trains quadriceps and hip extensors in pain-controlled environment
main_work.load_guidance: Load 60–70% of both-leg max. Cue: center the working foot and control the descent. Stop set if pelvis shifts or stance leg compensates.

main_work.name: Standing Single-Leg Leg Curl
main_work.purpose: Isolated hamstring concentric and eccentric work; builds confidence and side-to-side balance
main_work.load_guidance: Machine setting; start 50–60% of typical two-leg curl. Control the eccentric 2–3 sec. Stop if sharp pain appears; mild tightness is expected early in block.

main_work.name: Cable Hip Abduction
main_work.purpose: Lateral hip strength and single-leg stance control; supports winger cutting and deceleration mechanics
main_work.load_guidance: Light cable (3–5 kg). Cue: stand tall, light hand support, drive knee out and back. High-rep range builds motor control without fatigue.

cooldown.name: Inchworm Walkout
cooldown.purpose: Dynamic posterior-chain and shoulder mobility; transition from intense work to movement-based recovery

cooldown.name: World's Greatest Stretch
cooldown.purpose: Multi-joint mobility flow targeting hamstring, hip flexor, ankle, and thoracic range; prepare for position-specific demands

injury_modifications: If hamstring tightness or sharp pain appears during any exercise, stop set immediately and note range. Do not progress load that week.
Reduce B-stance RDL reps to 5–6 per side if soreness lingers post-session. Prioritize pain-free eccentric range over load.
If standing single-leg balance is poor, use light cable or dumbbell hold for hand support; do not force balance loss.

weeks.progression_rule: Start with controlled hinge (B-stance RDL) and single-leg machine work (leg press, leg curl) to build confidence and pain-free range. Monitor for tightness triggers; avoid sprinting.

program.nutrition_focus: Protein-adequate intake to support tissue repair (esp. hamstring eccentric load); carbohydrate timing around session for energy and glycogen; hydration emphasis given single high-demand session per week.
recovery_focus: Active recovery drills 2–3 days post-session to reduce stiffness and maintain mobility without adding fatigue
Restorative modalities (foam roll posterior chain, lacrosse ball on glutes/hamstring) on off-days to manage tightness early
Sleep consistency (7 h) and moderate stress management critical for single-session recovery and adaptation
safety_notes: No true 1RM tests or max-effort sprinting this week. Hamstring history requires conservative loading and pain-monitoring.
Eccentric loading on leg curl and RDL variant should feel controlled, never sharp. Mild muscle soreness 24–48 h post is acceptable; tightness or sharp pain requires assessment and load reduction.
Single-leg work relies on balance; ensure adequate hand support and light loading to prevent ankle/foot compensation.
Session is designed for 60 min: 5 min warmup (3 drills), 35 min main work (4 exercises ~8–9 min each), 10 min cooldown, 10 min buffer for transitions and breathing.
assumptions: Athlete has access to leg press and leg curl machines, cable machine, dumbbells/kettlebells, and space for mobility drills.
Previous hamstring tightness is resolved or asymptomatic at rest; no active inflammation or medical contraindication to controlled eccentric loading.
Athlete is familiar with basic hinge mechanics and single-leg stance from prior training; coaching on form available before first session.
Moderate stress and 7 h sleep baseline are maintained throughout the week to support tissue adaptation.
No upcoming matches or high-intensity team practice this week; single session is only lower-body stimulus to minimize cumulative hamstring load.
